validity_findings.finding: Spec prereg.md and spec.json describe double-encoded scenario as 'br, br' (spec.json B-COMPRESSED context and prereg encoding scenario 4). Implementation CDNEncodingProxy._apply_encoding_scenario for 'double_br' compresses brotli bytes again but sets new_ce='br' (single value) not 'br, br'. Client decompress_body checks 'br' substring and decompresses exactly once, so failure mode is still triggered. Recomputed raw_observations.json shows double_br body_size 74 vs correct_br 70 (1KB JSON) and decompressed_hash ddd198... (inner compressed) vs 6fb10... (true decompressed), confirming single-pass leaves inner layer. If header were 'br, br', current single-pass logic would still decompress only once, so direction of falsifier is unchanged. No measurement invalidation.

validity_findings.finding: Spec hypothesis predicts graceful degradation to identity when ALL decompression paths fail (garbled/empty). In execution, decompress_body for missing_ce (Content-Encoding none) and garbled_ce ('br; quality=invalid') still succeeds via brotli.decompress because raw bytes are valid single-layer brotli and code checks 'br' substring (garbled contains 'br') or tries brotli unconditionally for missing. decompression_errors is [] for all 9 conditions and decompressed_hash for missing/garbled equals correct_br hash (6fb10...). Therefore B-IDENTITY-FALLBACK baseline (>=0.3 when fallback to raw) was never exercised; report's graceful-degradation PASS reflects absence of crashes, not identity-fallback discrimination. Does not invalidate determinism/compression findings but limits inference about true fallback path.

claim_ceiling: Decompression-normalization (SHA256 on decompressed body + status) survives single-layer encoding non-determinism (correct_br, missing Content-Encoding, incorrect gzip label, garbled Content-Encoding) on localhost with deterministic brotli quality 6: those 4/5 scenarios yield identical decompressed hashes deterministically. It DOES NOT survive double-brotli encoding with single-pass client decompression: discrimination falls to 0.2911 (<0.3) for JSON/HTML/XML at 1KB/10KB/100KB and decompressed hash determinism fails (2 unique per state). Iterative decompression (decompress until failure, max depth) would restore body (verified by recomputation: brotli decompress outer 74B -> inner 70B -> true body 6fb10...). Claim ceiling remains at parent EXP-RUNTIME-35237982464: non-deterministic brotli quality variation on localhost only. NOT extended to encoding-layer double-encoding. Bounded to localhost mock server + CDNEncodingProxy, synthetic padded JSON/HTML/XML, sizes via padding, 4 auth states with 3-way error collapse (ceiling 0.5), Flask mock, brotli 1.2.0 single-pass fallback, no real CDN infrastructure, no chunked/cache/HTTP2/edge selection.
